subject: Use names attribute of lists inside a l*ply function

messages.author: 7e54aa65e5af5819
messages.subject: Use names attribute of lists inside a l*ply function
parts:
I would like to use in a function passed to l*ply the names attribute
of lists or in the case of lists generated by *lply the values of attr
(,"split_labels"). In the example below that would be the id variables
"first" and "second", but it seems that these attributes are dropped
after l*ply starts processing the lists.

It would be greatly appreciated if somebody could point me in the
right direction, as most probably the list references are not correct.

Thanks.

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com


> library(plyr)
> id <- c("first", "second")
> variable <- c("a", "b")
> df <- expand.grid(id = id, variable = variable)
> dfl <- dlply(df, .(id), data.frame)
> dfl
$first
id variable
1 first a
3 first b

$second
id variable
2 second a
4 second b

attr(,"split_type")
[1] "data.frame"
attr(,"split_labels")
id
1 first
2 second
> names(dfl)
[1] "first" "second"
> l_ply(dfl, function(x){print(attr(x,"split_labels"))})
NULL
NULL
> l_ply(dfl, function(x){print(names(x))})
[1] "id" "variable"
[1] "id" "variable"

messages.subject: Re: Use names attribute of lists inside a l*ply function
parts:
I am working on a report, and am aiming to generate many latex/html
tables using a combination of l_ply and xtable. In order to
distinguish from which list the table was generated it would be nice
to automatically specify the caption argument for xtable which is the
name of the list (a and b in the example below).

a <- data.frame(s1 = c(runif(3)))
b <- data.frame(s1 = c(sample(100,2)))
e <- list(a=a,b=b)

l_ply(e, function(x){
xtable(x[1])
}, .print = TRUE)

--
http://learnr.wordpress.com

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Use names attribute of lists inside a l*ply function
parts: Ah, in that case I'd use m_ply and explicitly pass in the names:

library(xtable)
m_ply(cbind(data = e, name = names(e)), function(data, name){
xtable(data[1], caption = name)
}, .print = TRUE)

Hadley
